summary.intent: Merge PR #537 (module-resolution fix) once the desktop E2E run came back green.
summary.outcome: PR #537's fix was confirmed working (E2E failures dropped 4→1), but a separate pre-existing FUSE publish-coordination race causes move-content to fail on all platforms; PR #537 was held. A diagnostics improvement was committed to #537, and a separate FUSE fix PR was started.

repo: Desktop E2E has been failing since #532/#533 landed; 'green' main branch CI runs simply skipped desktop via path filters — only workflow_dispatch forces all suites, creating a false impression of green CI.

The FUSE mkdir parent-publish snapshots root children at callback time and does a blind overwrite with no merge on success; merge only fires on a 409 conflict, which never happens because both publishers serialize on the same coordinator lock (so the second writer gets a valid sequence and succeeds silently).

move-content is the only E2E scenario with back-to-back writeFileSync(root) → mkdirSync(root subdir), which is what triggers the latent concurrent-publisher race; cross-client-sync passes because it never does that interleaving.
#533 substantially touched the publish machinery (lib.rs +511, journal_helpers.rs +152) even though it didn't originate the race — the race is a latent defect that predates both #532 and #533.

code.finding: mkdir parent-publish takes a snapshot of root children at callback time and launches it in a background thread — stale if a concurrent file-write added children after the snapshot.
mkdir Success arm does coordinator.record_publish(parent, new_seq) with no merge — blind overwrite that silently drops concurrent changes.
coordinator.get_lock(root_ipns) serializes publishers so no 409 is generated, preventing the merge path from ever firing.
merge_folder_children exists and is correct but is only invoked on a 409 conflict response, which the lock prevents.
coordinator.get_lock(root_ipns) — same lock used by both mkdir and file-write publishers, causing silent success instead of conflict.
spawn_metadata_publish (file-write debounced path) builds a fresh snapshot and merges on conflict — the mkdir path lacks this safety.
build_folder_metadata(parent_ino) called at mkdir callback time — the snapshot races with handle_create adding the file to root.children.
Verifier child stdout/stderr was swallowed (only exit code checked), making fresh-client resolve failures completely invisible and forcing a 3-strand investigation to diagnose.

workflow: Parallel multi-agent workflow investigation (4 agents, ~300k tokens) was effective for attributing a subtle race across Rust product code, test history, and CI logs simultaneously.
Attribution claims from deep investigation should be verified against source before acting — the workflow overstated '#533 didn't touch the publish path' when git diff showed +511/+152 lines.
When CI shows 'green' on a branch, check whether the relevant suite was actually skipped by path filters before concluding the change is safe.

friction: Desktop E2E job harness swallows the verifier child's stdout/stderr, reporting only exit code — made the actual fresh-client failure invisible and forced a multi-agent investigation to reconstruct it from circumstantial log evidence.
GHA path filtering created a false-green CI history on main, obscuring that desktop E2E had been broken since #532/#533 landed.

The move-content test's back-to-back write+mkdir interleaving is the only trigger for the race, but there was no comment or documentation explaining why that specific ordering matters — making the scenario's significance non-obvious.
open_items: FUSE publish-coordination lost-update race fix: make mkdir parent-publish go through the same merge-on-write debounced publisher as the file-write path (write_ops.rs:574-586 and 671-696), or at minimum merge_folder_children before the blind overwrite in the Success arm. Needs a separate fix(desktop) PR with a release bump.
PR #537 is held pending desktop E2E going fully green (requires the FUSE fix above to land first).
Consider adding a CI guard or comment to flag that workflow_dispatch is required to exercise desktop E2E — regular push runs silently skip it.
